title: Commonwealth Scholarship
university: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
deadline_note: Applications for the 2027/28 academic year close at 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October. Nominators may set their own closing dates and will nominate candidates to the CSC by December 2026. Applications may not be edited after submitting and no late applications are accepted.
application_cycle: 2027/28 academic year, with study in the UK beginning September/October 2027; nominators nominate to the CSC by December 2026 and applicants hear the outcome by July 2027
status_note: The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission states 'Applications for Commonwealth Master's Scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year are now open.'
tuition_coverage_note: The CSC states 'Approved tuition fees: full fees are covered by agreement between the CSC and the UK university, and Scholars are not liable to pay for any part of the tuition fee.'
benefits: Approved airfare from the Scholar's home country to the UK and return at the end of the award
Approved tuition fees - full fees covered by agreement between the CSC and the UK university, with Scholars not liable to pay any part of the tuition fee
Stipend (living allowance) at the rate of £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month for those at universities in the London metropolitan area
Study travel grant towards the cost of study-related travel within the UK or overseas

Child allowance of £622 per month for the first child and £154 per month for the second and third child under the age of 16, if the Scholar is widowed, divorced or a single parent and the children live with them
A full assessment of needs and eligibility for additional financial support if a Scholar shares that they have a disability
eligibility: Be a citizen of or have been granted refugee status by an eligible Commonwealth country, or be a British Protected Person
Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country
Be available to start academic studies in the UK by the start of the UK academic year in September 2027
By September 2027, hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours standard, or a lower second-class degree and a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a Master's degree)
Be unable to afford to study in the UK without this scholarship
Have provided all supporting documentation in the required format
requirements: Apply via CSC Central - the CSC is unable to accept any applications or documentation not submitted via CSC Central
Upload references from at least two individuals in PDF format by the deadline, either on institutional letterhead or an email clearly showing the sender's details
Upload proof of citizenship or refugee status: a copy of a valid passport or national ID card showing a photograph, date of birth and country of citizenship

Upload full transcripts detailing all higher education qualifications, including to-date transcripts for any courses currently being studied, with certified translations if not in English; applications will be considered ineligible if any transcripts are missing or do not include all pages
The CSC does not charge to apply for any of its scholarships or fellowships through its online application system
All Commonwealth Scholars commit to returning home following the end of their scholarships; switching to a graduate or other visa to remain in the UK is not permitted
coverage: Stipend living allowance at £1,712 per month (£2,000 in the London metropolitan area)
Approved airfare from home country to the UK and return
Study travel grant for study-related travel within the UK or overseas
application_method: Apply through the online application system CSC Central, and separately to a national nominating agency or an invited NGO or charitable body nominator
application_route: Apply via CSC Central and separately to a national nominating agency (the main route) or an invited NGO/charitable body nominator; the CSC does not accept direct applications. Nominators may set their own closing dates and nominate to the CSC by December 2026.
study_mode: Full-time study only; no other course of study may be undertaken at the same time
duration: One year - the CSC funds one-year taught Master's programmes only and does not fund MBA degrees
description: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships enable talented and motivated individuals to gain the knowledge and skills required for sustainable development, and are aimed at those who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK, for candidates from eligible low and middle income Commonwealth countries to undertake full-time taught Master's study at a UK university.

not_confirmed: deadline_date for the nominators' separate closing dates
verification.notes: Benefits, eligibility criteria, application process, selection criteria, tenure and financial assistance were read directly from the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission's official page for Commonwealth Master's Scholarships. The page lists 43 eligible Commonwealth countries and states that in line with the commitments made at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) 2024, the Commission particularly welcomes applications from Small Island Developing States. The application deadline for the 2027/28 academic year is 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October, with study in the UK beginning September/October 2027. The stipend rate of £1,712 per month (£2,000 in the London metropolitan area) is quoted by the CSC at current levels and is subject to change. Family allowances are described by the CSC as only a contribution towards the cost of maintaining a Scholar's family in the UK, and the true costs are likely to be considerably higher. This record covers the Master's Scholarships only; the Commonwealth PhD Scholarships scheme is a separate award and should not be confused with it. Nominators may set their own closing dates and may have additional eligibility criteria, and a nomination is no guarantee of selection.

applicant_utility: The Commonwealth Master's Scholarship covers everything a UK master's student normally has to find money for: approved airfare home to the UK and return, your full tuition fees under an agreement between the CSC and your university, a living allowance of £1,712 a month (£2,000 if your university is in the London metropolitan area), a study travel grant for research travel, and child allowances if you are a single parent or widowed. Because these benefits are quoted at current levels, expect the figures to be updated slightly each cycle. The route in matters more than the deadline: you cannot apply directly to the CSC. You apply through a national nominating agency, or an invited NGO or charitable body, and nominators set their own earlier closing dates and may add extra eligibility rules, so the 20 October 2026 CSC deadline is not the one to build your calendar around. Selections are made only from the pool of nominations, and a nomination is no guarantee of selection. Selection turns on three things - your own merit including academic experience, the quality of your research proposal, and the potential impact on the development of your home country - so write the Development Impact section of the form as carefully as your academic credentials. Two hard eligibility rules: you must hold a first degree of at least upper second-class standard by September 2027, and if you have already studied at master's level in the UK or already held a Commonwealth Scholarship at master's level you will not be considered.
